one_line: Rival Mughal princes Bahadur Shah I (Muazzam) and Azam Shah, locked in the 1707 succession struggle at Jajau.

appearance.age_look: Bahadur Shah I appears in his late 40s–50s with a dignified medium build; Azam Shah appears in his late 30s–40s with a lean, proud warrior’s build.
appearance.face: Bahadur Shah has an oval face, wheatish complexion, neatly trimmed black beard with a few grey strands, calm sharp eyes with slight crow’s feet and a composed, thoughtful default expression; Azam Shah has a slightly angular face, wheatish-olive complexion, well-groomed fuller black beard and moustache, intense narrow eyes and a firm, resolved default expression.
appearance.hair: Both keep their hair tied under turbans; Bahadur Shah wears a tall, slightly conical Mughal turban in deep emerald green with fine gold stripe edging and a central jewelled sarpech plume, while Azam Shah wears a slightly lower-profile Mughal turban in rich crimson with narrow cream banding and a smaller curved jewelled sarpech plume.
appearance.costume: Bahadur Shah wears a long, knee-length Mughal jama of soft cream-coloured silk with fine diagonal wrap, slim sleeves and a subtle gold floral jaal pattern, tied with a broad deep-green silk patka sash embroidered with thin gold thread at the edges, over straight white cotton paijama trousers and soft brown leather mojari shoes; over his jama he dons a sleeveless quilted khaki-brown cotton brigandine-style coat lightly studded with small metal rivets, hinting at battlefield readiness, and a simple jade-bead necklace with a small gold pendant at his chest; Azam Shah wears a slightly shorter, wrap-style jama in rich pale-blue silk with delicate darker-blue buta motifs, tied with a wide crimson patka sash bearing thin woven gold chevrons, over off-white paijama trousers and dark tan mojari shoes, plus a slightly darker blue quilted cotton-over-mail coat with subtle horizontal stitching and a few visible ring-mail edges at the arms, and he carries a modest string of dark prayer beads around his left wrist.
appearance.signature: Bahadur Shah’s signature prop is a sheathed, gently curved Mughal talwar with a dark steel hilt and small red stone set in the pommel, hanging from his green patka on his left hip, while Azam Shah’s signature prop is a drawn, polished Mughal talwar with a slightly broader blade, ornate gilt hilt and a slim red tassel at the pommel held in his right hand.

ref_desc: Bahadur Shah I has an oval wheatish face with a trimmed black-and-grey beard, emerald turban, cream-and-gold jama, green sash and sheathed talwar, while Azam Shah has an angular wheatish-olive face with fuller beard, crimson turban, pale-blue jama, red sash and drawn talwar, all in Mughal battlefield attire.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two Mughal princes at the 1707 Battle of Jajau, shown side by side for comparison: Bahadur Shah I on the left and Azam Shah on the right, both fully clothed in dignified, era-accurate Mughal battlefield attire. Bahadur Shah I has an oval wheatish face, calm sharp eyes and a neatly trimmed black beard with a few grey strands, his default expression composed and thoughtful; his hair is covered by a tall, slightly conical emerald-green Mughal turban edged with fine gold stripes and adorned with a central jewelled sarpech plume. He wears a long, cream-coloured silk jama with a diagonal wrap, slim sleeves and subtle gold floral jaal pattern, tied with a wide deep-green silk patka sash embroidered with thin gold thread at the edges, over straight white cotton paijama trousers and soft brown leather mojari shoes; over this, he has a sleeveless quilted khaki-brown cotton brigandine-style coat lightly studded with tiny metal rivets, plus a simple jade-bead necklace with a small gold pendant. His signature weapon is a sheathed, gently curved Mughal talwar hanging from his green patka on his left hip, with a dark steel hilt and a small red stone in the pommel, kept at a relaxed but ready angle. Azam Shah has a slightly angular wheatish-olive face with intense narrow eyes, a fuller well-groomed black beard and moustache, and a firm, resolved default expression; his hair is wrapped in a lower-profile crimson Mughal turban with narrow cream banding and a smaller curved jewelled sarpech plume. He wears a slightly shorter wrap-style pale-blue silk jama with delicate darker-blue buta motifs, tied with a broad crimson patka sash woven with thin gold chevrons, over off-white paijama trousers and dark tan mojari shoes; over his jama, he dons a slightly darker blue quilted cotton-over-mail coat with subtle horizontal stitching and hints of ring-mail showing at the arms, and a string of dark prayer beads around his left wrist. His signature weapon is a drawn polished Mughal talwar with a slightly broader blade, ornate gilt hilt and a slim red tassel at the pommel held firmly in his right hand. Use a rich but grounded palette of emerald green, cream, gold, crimson and pale blue, and show both figures head-to-toe with clear views of their turbans, faces, sashes, weapons and footwear for consistent redrawing, keeping the scene family-safe and historically grounded without fantasy elements.
